prompt: Polarising sunglasses cut glare from a wet road much better than ordinary tinted lenses. Why?

options.text: Light reflected from a flat surface is partly polarised horizontally, and the lenses are oriented to block that horizontal component
They block all blue light, and glare is mostly blue
They reflect the glare back because their surface is mirrored
They make the pupil contract, so less glare is noticed

explanation: Reflection from horizontal surfaces polarises light mainly in the horizontal plane. Polarising lenses have a vertical transmission axis, so they selectively block that reflected horizontal glare while letting other light through.
